cautions: Precision systems like GPS also need relativity corrections; don't claim Newton's maths is the whole story.
Draw an original Newton-inspired character only if style allows; no copyrighted portraits.

ideas.title: Closest to the Sun in January
ideas.hook: On 3 January, Earth is closer to the Sun than on any other day of the year.
ideas.angle: Seasons come from Earth's tilt, not its distance from the Sun, and near the equator in Sri Lanka the yearly rhythm is set by monsoons instead.
ideas.why_now: Earth reaches perihelion on 3 January 2027 at 02:33 UT (08:03 Sri Lanka time).

sources.title: Earth's Seasons and Apsides, 2027 (U.S. Naval Observatory)

research_leads: Get the perihelion/aphelion distances from USNO or JPL to show the small difference.
Use Sri Lanka Department of Meteorology climate data for the monsoon seasons.
cautions: Classic misconception; ensure the tilt explanation is visually clear.

ideas.title: Equal night? Not quite
ideas.hook: The equinox is supposed to mean equal day and night. It doesn't, not even in Sri Lanka.
ideas.angle: What the equinox really is (the Sun crossing the celestial equator) and why sunrise/sunset definitions and refraction make daylight a little longer than 12 hours.
ideas.why_now: March equinox: 20 March 2027 at 20:25 UT (01:55 on 21 March, Sri Lanka time).

sources.title: Earth's Seasons and Apsides, 2027 (U.S. Naval Observatory)

research_leads: Get Colombo sunrise/sunset times for 20-21 March 2027 from USNO to show day length.
Check the definition of sunrise (upper limb, refraction) on USNO.
cautions: Local date is 21 March in Sri Lanka; state time zones.

ideas.title: What '70% chance of rain' really means
ideas.hook: Your weather app says 70% chance of rain. Most people get that number wrong.
ideas.angle: How forecasters run many simulations (ensembles) to turn uncertain weather into a probability, and how that helps warnings for Sri Lanka's monsoons.
ideas.why_now: World Meteorological Day is 23 March; the 2027 theme is 'Trusted Science. Better Forecasts. Safer World.'

sources.title: World Meteorological Day | WMO
List of International Days and Weeks (United Nations)

research_leads: Verify the definition of probability of precipitation from a national met service.
Ask Sri Lanka's Department of Meteorology how they issue monsoon and cyclone warnings.
cautions: Disaster warnings are safety-critical; tell viewers to follow official alerts.

ideas.title: The man inside every battery
ideas.hook: Alessandro Volta died 200 years ago, and his name is printed on every battery you own.
ideas.angle: How Volta's pile made the first steady electric current from stacked metals and wet layers, and how today's batteries (some using graphite like Sri Lanka's) work on the same idea.
ideas.why_now: 200th anniversary of Volta's death on 5 March 1827; Como, Pavia and Milan run a bicentenary programme through 2027.

sources.title: Volta, Alessandro (Biblioteca Digitale, Università di Pavia)
200VOLTeVOLTA - Alessandro Volta bicentenary (Fondazione Alessandro Volta)

research_leads: Pavia page: Volta announced his 'artificial electric organ' (the pile) in a letter to Joseph Banks dated 20 March 1800; confirm with Royal Society records.
Verify that the SI unit volt is named after him (BIPM SI brochure).
Check Sri Lanka vein graphite and its use in battery anodes with the Geological Survey and Mines Bureau.
cautions: Don't show batteries being opened or short-circuited (safety).
Graphite-in-batteries link is a lead only until sourced.

ideas.title: Hello, London? The first public call across the ocean
ideas.hook: 100 years ago, a phone call crossed the Atlantic with no cable at all.
ideas.angle: How the 1927 transatlantic telephone service sent voices by radio between transmitter and receiving stations, and how today's calls ride undersea fibre-optic cables instead.
ideas.why_now: 100th anniversary: the first official commercial transatlantic telephone call was made on 7 January 1927 between New York and London.

sources.title: First Official Transatlantic Telephone Call (January 7, 1927) - National Recording Registry essay by Cary O'Dell with Sheldon Hochheiser, Library of Congress
First Transatlantic Phone Call (IEEE Communications Society)

research_leads: LoC: route went New York - Rocky Point (radio) - Rugby, England; return via Cupar, Scotland - Houlton, Maine. Confirm with BT Archives.
Find which submarine cables land in Sri Lanka today for the modern half of the story (TeleGeography / operator pages).
cautions: The recording itself is historic audio; check rights before using any of it, or recreate with drawn characters and new voices.

ideas.title: AI is mostly multiplication
ideas.hook: Behind every AI chatbot answer is a mountain of school-level maths: multiply, add, repeat.
ideas.angle: How a neural network turns numbers into predictions using simple multiplication and addition repeated at enormous scale.
ideas.why_now: International Day of Mathematics is 14 March; the 2027 theme is 'Mathematics, AI and Our Future'.

sources.title: International Day of Mathematics (IDM)

research_leads: Confirm the IDM's UNESCO proclamation (2019) on unesco.org.
Have a machine-learning reviewer check the simplified neuron/weights explanation.
cautions: Avoid hype or fear about AI; keep claims modest and accurate.
Don't depict real AI products' branding or interfaces.

ideas.title: Do full moons really fill maternity wards?
ideas.hook: Ask around a maternity ward and someone will tell you babies love a full moon. We lined up ten years of daily births to check.
ideas.angle: How to test a folk claim with data: match every day's births to the Moon's phase and see whether full-moon days stand out from ordinary day-to-day noise.
ideas.why_now: Each month of the quarter has a Poya full-moon holiday in Sri Lanka (Duruthu, Navam, Medin), so the full moon is already on viewers' calendars; Poya days stay public and bank holidays in 2027.

sources.title: The effect of the lunar cycle on frequency of births and birth complications (Arliss, Kaplan, Galvin, Am J Obstet Gynecol 192(5):1462-1464)
2027 public and bank holidays gazetted (Daily Mirror)

research_leads: Get exact full-moon dates and times for 1994-2014 from the USNO moon-phases data service (aa.usno.navy.mil, 'public information') and assign each birth date a lunar phase.
Confirm the Arliss et al. 2005 result (564,039 North Carolina births, 1997-2001, 62 lunar cycles, no significant difference across 8 phases) from the full paper.
Check whether the SSA 2000-2014 file gives the same answer as the CDC/NCHS 1994-2003 file, and whether weekday and holiday effects (scheduled births) are larger than any lunar effect.
Confirm 2027 Poya dates (Duruthu, Navam, Medin) in the 2027 holiday gazette; search results gave Duruthu Poya as 22 January 2027 but the Central Bank page could not be opened.
Look for openly licensed Sri Lankan daily birth registrations; none were found or checked for licence.
cautions: Pregnancy and birth topic: no medical advice, and nothing that could worry expectant parents.
The data are US births, not Sri Lankan; say so on screen.
Planned inductions and caesareans move births to weekdays, which can hide or fake patterns; explain this rather than over-claim.
Treat Poya and other lunar beliefs respectfully; the film tests a maternity-ward myth, not religious practice.

data.source: FiveThirtyEight 'births' dataset: US daily births 1994-2003 (CDC/NCHS) and 2000-2014 (Social Security Administration)
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, the fivethirtyeight/data repository LICENSE); the underlying CDC/NCHS and SSA counts are US government works
data.check: Arliss et al. 2005: 564,039 births over 62 lunar cycles showed no significant differences in birth frequency across the eight lunar phases.

ideas.title: Where did Sri Lanka's extra 24 years of life come from?
ideas.hook: A baby born in Sri Lanka in 1950 could expect to live about 53 years. A baby born in 2023? About 77.
ideas.angle: What 'life expectancy at birth' really measures (an average pulled down by early deaths), and which ages Sri Lanka's gains came from, by comparing UN life tables across decades.
ideas.why_now: Our World in Data's life-expectancy chart lists its next update for 2 December 2026, so the newest UN-based numbers should be out just before the quarter; UN WPP is revised every two years (latest confirmed: 2024).

sources.title: World Population Prospects 2024: Summary of Results (UN DESA Population Division)
Life expectancy (Long-run data), Our World in Data

research_leads: Download WPP 2024 abridged life tables for Sri Lanka and decompose the 1950-2023 gain by age group, to test (not assume) how much came from fewer deaths of young children.
Check whether a WPP 2026 revision has been released and whether it changes Sri Lanka's figures.
OWID chart (WPP 2024) values to re-check: Sri Lanka 53.2 years (1950) and 77.5 (2023); India 72.0 and world 73.2 in 2023.
Compare with Sri Lanka's own vital registration figures (Registrar General / Department of Census and Statistics) and note their licence before use.
Look at the 2020-2021 COVID-19 dip and whether it shows in the Sri Lanka series.
cautions: Child and maternal deaths are sensitive; keep the tone factual and avoid images of sick children.
Life expectancy at birth is not how long any one person will live; make that clear to avoid misreading.
WPP values are modelled estimates and change between revisions.
Avoid crediting a single policy for the gains unless the film's research supports it.

data.source: UN DESA Population Division, World Population Prospects 2024 (life expectancy and life tables)
data.terms: CC BY 3.0 IGO (Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO, stated in the WPP 2024 Summary of Results); OWID's own charts are CC BY 4.0
data.check: WPP 2024 Summary of Results: global life expectancy at birth reached 73.3 years in 2024, up 8.4 years since 1995.

ideas.title: The season Sri Lanka's rice harvest crashed
ideas.hook: In one season, Sri Lanka's rice harvest fell by more than a third. Same fields, same farmers. What changed was the fertiliser.
ideas.angle: Why rice plants need nitrogen and other nutrients, and what national paddy data show for output and yield before, during and after the 2021 chemical-fertiliser import ban.
ideas.why_now: The 2026/27 Maha harvest falls in or near the quarter, five years after the 2021/22 Maha season; the film can compare the new season with the crash year.

sources.title: National average rice yield hits nearly 50-year-low in Maha season amid fertiliser ban (Daily Mirror)

research_leads: Get the Department of Census and Statistics paddy statistics by season (Maha 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23) to separate the two seasons that FAOSTAT's annual totals combine.
Re-check the DCS figures reported by Daily Mirror: Maha 2021/22 output down 37% to 1.93 million tonnes, average yield down 33.76% from 2020/21 Maha, harvested area 766,000 ha.
Compare with the HARTI farmer survey, which search results say found yield falls of over 50%; explain why survey and national figures differ.
Confirm the ban's start (May 2021) and reversal (November 2021) dates from primary government sources.
Confirm the 2026/27 Maha harvest timing with the Department of Agriculture.
cautions: Politically charged; show data and plant science, not blame of named politicians.
Weather, fuel shortages and the 2022 economic crisis also affected farming; don't credit all of the fall to fertiliser without evidence.
Don't present organic farming as good or bad in general; this was a sudden nationwide switch.
Farmers' livelihoods were hit hard; keep the tone respectful.

data.source: FAOSTAT Crops and livestock products (QCL): rice (paddy) area, yield and production, Sri Lanka
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, per FAO Database terms of use for corporate statistical databases such as FAOSTAT)
data.check: Department of Census and Statistics via Daily Mirror (2022-11-14): 2021/22 Maha paddy output fell 37% to 1.93 million tonnes and average yield fell 33.76% versus 2020/21 Maha.

ideas.title: Is most of the world's cinnamon from Sri Lanka?
ideas.hook: 'Most of the world's cinnamon comes from Sri Lanka.' You've heard it. Let's check the numbers.
ideas.angle: Two different trees are sold as 'cinnamon': true (Ceylon) cinnamon and cassia. Whether the claim is right depends on which one you count, and world statistics may lump them together.
ideas.why_now: No fixed date; an evergreen myth-buster with a strong Sri Lankan angle that can fill a gap in the quarter.

sources.title: Ceylon Cinnamon reigns supreme in the global Cinnamon market (Sri Lanka Export Development Board blog)
2022 Cinnamon Report (Tridge)

research_leads: Confirm in FAOSTAT's item definitions whether 'Cinnamon and cinnamon-tree flowers, raw' includes cassia species.
Compute Sri Lanka's share of FAOSTAT world 'cinnamon' production over time, then compare with the EDB claims (70% of global pure-cinnamon production; over 85% of the world market for true cinnamon).
Find an independent source for true-cinnamon versus cassia production (e.g. a botanical or trade study) rather than relying on export-promotion figures.
Check the 2015 Piyasiri & Wijeratne study on Sri Lanka's cinnamon market share (2000-2013), reported in search results but not opened.
cautions: EDB and trade-site figures are promotional or unsourced; treat them as claims to test, not facts.
Avoid health claims about cinnamon or cassia (e.g. coumarin) unless separately sourced.
Don't show real brand packaging or logos.

data.source: FAOSTAT Crops and livestock products (QCL): cinnamon production by country
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, per FAO Database terms of use for FAOSTAT)
data.check: Tridge (2022-03-11): Indonesia, China, Vietnam and Sri Lanka together produced 98% of world cinnamon in 2020.

ideas.title: The winter visitors in Sri Lanka's skies
ideas.hook: Some of the birds in Sri Lanka this January don't live here. Bird-watchers' records show when they arrive and when they leave.
ideas.angle: How migration shows up in data: plot month-by-month sightings of a winter migrant in Sri Lanka from eBird records to show the August-to-April season and the spring departure.
ideas.why_now: January to March is the second half of the migrant season, and departures begin around March, so viewers can still see the birds before they go.

sources.title: As birds winter in Sri Lanka, one enthusiast makes sure their memory stays (Mongabay)
EOD - eBird Observation Dataset (GBIF)

research_leads: Choose one or two clearly migratory species with a Sri Lankan ornithologist (e.g. Field Ornithology Group of Sri Lanka) and confirm their status.
Normalise sightings by number of checklists per month so that tourist-season birding effort doesn't fake a peak.
Check the 2009 Taprobanica avifauna checklist, which search results say lists 203 purely migrant species, against Mongabay's 'more than 200'.
Mongabay says some species (e.g. brown shrike) arrive in early to mid October and others leave in March; confirm with the data.
cautions: Observer effort varies a lot by month and place; say that the counts are records, not bird numbers.
Don't show exact locations of sensitive or threatened species.
If other GBIF datasets are added, keep only CC0 or CC BY records and drop CC BY-NC ones.
Birds should be drawn as original characters, not traced from photos.

data.source: GBIF: EOD - eBird Observation Dataset (Cornell Lab of Ornithology), occurrences in Sri Lanka
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (dataset licence as recorded by the GBIF API: creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0)
data.check: Mongabay (2019-10-25): more than 200 migratory bird species visit Sri Lanka from early August through April.

ideas.title: How hot is too hot for a coral?
ideas.hook: Corals are animals, and a few weeks of too-warm water can turn a whole reef white.
ideas.angle: What NOAA's 'Degree Heating Weeks' count, and how often the reefs off Sri Lanka have crossed the bleaching-alert thresholds since 1985.
ideas.why_now: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center (8 October 2026) says a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027, and NOAA warned in June 2026 that El Niño could bring widespread bleaching back.

sources.title: World's Fourth Mass Coral Bleaching Event Likely Ended in 2025 (NOAA NESDIS)
NOAA Coral Reef Watch Satellite Virtual Stations Time Series Graph Description
ENSO Diagnostic Discussion (NOAA Climate Prediction Center)

research_leads: List which CRW regional virtual stations cover Sri Lanka (an 'Eastern Sri Lanka' station appears in CRW alert pages) and download their daily DHW series.
Count years with DHW of 4 or more (Alert Level 1) and 8 or more (Alert Level 2) and check them against bleaching reports from Sri Lankan marine scientists (e.g. 1998, 2016, 2024).
Check whether Indian Ocean warming tends to lag El Niño, and by how long, from peer-reviewed sources before linking the two on screen.
Confirm when Sri Lanka's seas are usually warmest from the CRW climatology in the station file.
cautions: Satellite heat stress is not the same as observed bleaching; say 'heat stress' unless field reports confirm bleaching.
Don't forecast bleaching for a specific reef; give probabilities and NOAA's own wording.
Use drawn reefs, not real underwater footage.
Avoid doom framing; mention that corals can recover if heat stress is short.

data.source: NOAA Coral Reef Watch daily 5 km Regional Virtual Stations (SST, HotSpot, Degree Heating Week, alert level, 1985-present)
data.terms: NOAA/NESDIS STAR product disclaimer: 'Users are free to use the images or information hosted on this site as they wish' with credit to NOAA/NESDIS STAR (US government work)
data.check: NOAA NESDIS (2026-06-02): bleaching-level heat stress hit 84% of the world's coral reef area from early 2023 to mid-2025, with mass bleaching in at least 83 countries and territories. CRW thresholds: Alert Level 1 at DHW 4, Alert Level 2 at DHW 8.

ideas.title: Closest to the Sun, and it's winter?
ideas.hook: On 3 January 2027 Earth is the closest it gets to the Sun all year, and half the planet is in winter.
ideas.angle: Seasons come from Earth's tilt, not its distance: a short script compares the small change in sunlight from distance (about 7%) with the much bigger change from tilt, and shows why near the equator, where Sri Lanka is, the year runs on monsoons more than winter and summer.
ideas.why_now: Perihelion is on 3 January 2027 at 02:33 UTC (08:03 in Sri Lanka), at the very start of the quarter; the March equinox (20 March 2027, 20:25 UTC) closes it.

sources.title: Milankovitch (Orbital) Cycles and Their Role in Earth's Climate (NASA Science)

research_leads: Pull perihelion, aphelion and equinox dates for 2027 from the USNO Earth's Seasons service and Earth-Sun distances from JPL Horizons or the NASA Earth Fact Sheet.
Compute noon sunlight intensity over the year for Colombo and for a high-latitude city to show tilt versus distance.
Check with the Sri Lanka Department of Meteorology which months are hottest in Colombo before saying so on screen.
Re-check NASA's figures: perihelion about 3 January, aphelion about 4 July, a 5.1 million km (3.4%) difference and about 6.8% more incoming sunlight in January than July.
cautions: A very common misconception; avoid mocking viewers who believed it.
Keep orbit diagrams to scale or clearly say they are not (the orbit is nearly a circle).
Don't claim specific Sri Lankan weather for a date.

data.source: US Naval Observatory Earth's Seasons data service (equinoxes, solstices, perihelion and aphelion, 1700-2100)
data.terms: Public information, US government work: USNO site notice says 'All information on this site is considered public information and may be distributed or copied unless otherwise specified' (credit requested)
data.check: NASA Science: perihelion on or about 3 January; perihelion-aphelion difference about 5.1 million km (3.4%); about 6.8% more incoming solar radiation in January than July. USNO API: perihelion 2027-01-03 02:33 UTC.

ideas.title: Why the sky is filling up with satellites
ideas.hook: In 2016 the world launched about 220 satellites. In 2025 it launched more than 4,500.
ideas.angle: What changed: cheap, mass-produced small satellites and huge constellations, shown by counting objects per year and per orbit in an open catalogue of everything launched.
ideas.why_now: Jonathan McDowell's yearly summary for 2025 is dated 4 February 2026, so a 2026 summary may land in the quarter (not confirmed); his GCAT catalogue was last updated 1 November 2026.

sources.title: Space Activities in 2025 (Jonathan McDowell, Rev 1.4)
GCAT: General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (Jonathan's Space Report)

research_leads: Count GCAT payloads by launch year and orbit class (LEO, SSO, GEO) and check against McDowell's Table 4 (payloads launched per year).
Look up Sri Lanka's first satellite (Raavana-1, a CubeSat) in GCAT to add a local beat; not yet verified.
Compare with other counts (e.g. Space.com: SpaceX 165 orbital flights in 2025) and explain why totals differ.
Check debris numbers (32,207 catalogued objects in orbit at end of 2025) and what share are working satellites.
cautions: Counts differ by definition (launches, payloads, catalogued objects); always say which one is shown.
Don't draw real company logos or rockets with branding.
Discuss space debris without alarmism; avoid claims about collision risk unless sourced.

data.source: GCAT: General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (Jonathan McDowell)
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (page states 'Licence: CC-BY-4.0 Creative Commons/Attribution')
data.check: McDowell, Space Activities in 2025: 329 orbital launch attempts (321 reaching orbit); 4,526 payloads launched in 2025 versus 221 in 2016; 32,207 catalogued objects in orbit at end of 2025.

ideas.title: How El Niño reaches Sri Lanka's rain
ideas.hook: A patch of warm water on the far side of the planet may be changing how much rain falls on Sri Lanka this season.
ideas.angle: Using satellite-plus-gauge rainfall for Sri Lanka and NOAA's El Niño index, compare October-December and January-March rain in past El Niño years with other years.
ideas.why_now: NOAA CPC (8 October 2026) is under an El Niño Advisory and says a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027; the ONI for July-September 2026 was +2.16.

sources.title: ENSO Diagnostic Discussion (NOAA Climate Prediction Center)
Identifying El Niño-Southern Oscillation influences on rainfall with classification models: implications for water resource management of Sri Lanka (De Silva & Hornberger, HESS 23, 1905-1929)

research_leads: Average CHIRPS rainfall over Sri Lanka (or the Mahaweli and Kelani basins) for Oct-Dec and Jan-Mar, 1981 to now, and split by ONI El Niño years.
Re-check De Silva & Hornberger's finding: during El Niño, rainfall rises in October-December and falls in the following January-March.
Read Zubair & Ropelewski (2006, J. Climate 19:1567-1575) on the strengthening ENSO-northeast monsoon link; the abstract was not reachable.
Add the Indian Ocean Dipole as a second driver, and check the November 2026 CPC update (due 12 November 2026).
cautions: Not a weather forecast: speak in tendencies and probabilities, not 'there will be floods' or 'drought'.
Floods and droughts hurt people; avoid real disaster footage and keep advice to official sources.
El Niño is one driver among several; past patterns may not repeat.

data.source: CHIRPS v2 daily/monthly rainfall (UCSB Climate Hazards Center) with NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ONI)
data.terms: CHIRPS: public domain ('Pete Peterson has waived all copyright and related or neighboring rights to CHIRPS'; 'in the public domain as registered with Creative Commons'). ONI: NOAA/NWS information in the public domain (weather.gov disclaimer)
data.check: De Silva & Hornberger 2019: during El Niño events rainfall increases in October-December and decreases in January-March in Sri Lanka's Mahaweli and Kelani basins. CPC: ONI JAS 2026 = +2.16; Niño-3.4 +2.1°C in September 2026.

ideas.title: How much has Sri Lanka warmed?
ideas.hook: 2023 to 2025 were, on average, more than 1.5 °C warmer than pre-industrial times, the first three-year stretch on record to do that. So what about Sri Lanka?
ideas.angle: Global averages hide local differences: pull reanalysis temperatures for the grid cells over Sri Lanka and compare its warming since 1940 with the global trend.
ideas.why_now: Copernicus releases its Global Climate Highlights each January (the 2025 edition came out on 14 January 2026), so the 2026 verdict should land at the start of the quarter.

sources.title: 2025 was the third-warmest year on record, Copernicus data show (ECMWF)
ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present (Copernicus Climate Data Store)

research_leads: Use ERA5 monthly 2 m temperature over land cells only (Sri Lanka is small next to the 0.25° grid; mask the sea).
Compare with Sri Lanka Department of Meteorology station records, checking their licence first.
Also look at warm nights (minimum temperatures), which may matter more for health; source any health claims separately.
Re-check the headline figures in the January 2027 Copernicus release before scripting.
cautions: Reanalysis is a model-data blend, not thermometer readings; say so simply.
Avoid alarmist framing, and don't give heat-health advice without a health source.
Don't confuse a single year's anomaly with the long-term Paris 1.5 °C limit (which refers to 20-year averages).

data.source: Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5 reanalysis (2 m temperature, 1940-present)
data.terms: CC-BY licence (as listed on the Climate Data Store dataset page)
data.check: ECMWF/Copernicus (2026-01-14): 2025 was 1.47 °C above 1850-1900 and third-warmest; 2024 was 1.60 °C; 2023-2025 averaged more than 1.5 °C.

ideas.title: AI's appetite for computing, by the numbers
ideas.hook: The computing power used to train the biggest AI models has been growing about five times every year.
ideas.angle: What 'training compute' means, and what growing 5x a year does over a few years, re-plotted from an open database of notable AI models.
ideas.why_now: The database was updated on 2 November 2026 and keeps adding new models, so the film can use the newest frontier models; AI tools are now part of how teenage viewers study.

sources.title: Trends in AI (Epoch AI)
Data on AI models (Epoch AI)

research_leads: Fit a log-linear trend to training compute for frontier models since 2020 and check it against Epoch's 5x per year (90% CI 4-6x; doubling every 4.6-6.0 months).
Turn FLOP into a viewer-friendly comparison (e.g. years of a phone's processor), checking the phone figure from a separate source.
Check how Epoch estimates compute for closed models and how uncertain those estimates are.
cautions: Compute for closed models is estimated, not reported; show error bars or say 'about'.
Don't equate compute with intelligence or make predictions about AI abilities.
No real company logos or branded chatbot characters; energy or water claims need their own sources.

data.source: Epoch AI, Data on AI models (notable AI models: training compute, parameters, dates)
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution; 'free to use, distribute, and reproduce provided the source and authors are credited')
data.check: Epoch AI Trends (updated 2026-02-05): training compute for frontier language models has grown about 5x per year since 2020.

ideas.title: Sri Lanka's rooftops vs its dams
ideas.hook: Sri Lanka's rooftop solar panels can now push out more power at once than all its big hydro dams. So why do the dams still make about three times more electricity?
ideas.angle: The difference between capacity (megawatts: how much at once) and energy (gigawatt-hours: how much over a year), and why sunshine hours set how much a solar panel really makes.
ideas.why_now: Full-year 2026 electricity figures start appearing early in the year, and rooftop solar is still growing fast; the film can show the newest totals. (Check whether January-March is a high-output solar period in Sri Lanka before saying so.)

sources.title: Renewable Generation Report, Quarter 04 2025 (Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka)
Electricity Data Explorer (Ember)

research_leads: Ember's yearly file covers Sri Lanka: solar 0.34 TWh (2.0%) in 2019 rising to 1.40 TWh (8.0%) in 2024; check for 2025 values.
PUCSL Q4 2025: at 31 Dec 2025, rooftop solar capacity 2,120 MW (CEB) + 352 MW (LECO) versus major hydro 1,533 MW; 2025 generation: rooftop solar 1,938 GWh versus major hydro 6,306 GWh.
Compute capacity factors (energy / (capacity x 8,760 h)) for solar and hydro and check them against published values.
Check the monthly pattern of solar output in Sri Lanka (PUCSL or CEB monthly data) before claiming any season is sunniest.
cautions: Solar tariffs and grid limits are live policy debates; explain the physics and avoid taking sides.
PUCSL and Ember totals may differ by method (e.g. rooftop solar estimates); say which is used.
Don't name or show installer companies or brands.

data.source: Ember yearly electricity data (generation, capacity and share by source; includes Sri Lanka)
data.terms: CC BY 4.0 (Ember: 'All content is released under a Creative Commons Attribution Licence (CC-BY-4.0)')
data.check: PUCSL Q4 2025 report: 2025 generation major hydro 6,306 GWh (35%), CEB coal 4,870 GWh (27%), NCRE 4,660 GWh (26%), thermal oil 2,216 GWh (12%); rooftop solar 1,938 GWh.
